newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore lifts travel ban on fugitive's wife.
newsitem.headline: Singapore lifts travel ban on fugitive's wife.

text.p: Singapore said on Wednesday it would return the passport of the wife of a fugitive opposition politician facing huge libel damages and let her travel abroad.
Teo Siew Har was barred from leaving Singapore in January when she tried to cross into Malaysia.
Officials said she was needed in Singapore to provide information on a tax investigation related to her husband, politician Tang Liang Hong. Tang now faces arrest on charges of tax evasion.

But Teo's daughter said her mother was unlikely to pay an early visit to Tang, who fled Singapore in January saying he had received death threats after losing in a bitterly contested general election.
"My mother has no immediate plans to meet with my father, not at this moment," Megan Tang told Reuters.
"I think she would like to see my brother who is now studying in England. She has not seen him for the past seven months," she said.
The Singapore Immigration Department said on Wednesday that Teo "has furnished the information requested of her".
Teo "may now be permitted to travel. Accordingly, she may apply to Singapore Immigration for her passport", it said in a statement.

On May 29 a Singapore court awarded Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and senior colleagues in his ruling party a record Singapore $8.08 million (US$5.65 million) in libel damages from Tang, who had called them liars when they accused him of being "an anti-English education, anti-Christian Chinese chauvinist".
Tang has said he would appeal the damages, and has other appeals pending. Since leaving Singapore, he has been in Malaysia, Britain and Hong Kong.
He was also formally charged on May 23 with 33 counts of tax evasion, and a warrant was issued for his arrest.
Tang faces a fine of three times the amount of tax he is accused of evading -- S$211,000 -- plus a fine of S$10,000 on each charge. He could also be jailed for three years on each charge.
Tang was reached in Hong Kong on Wednesday.
"Of course I'd like to meet her and she has missed her son," Tang said by telephone.

Tang said his wife had gone to court to claim back some of the family assets by the Singapore authorities. She says they are hers. Lawyers for Goh and the PAP leaders said she held the assets in trust for Tang.
